title: Duplicate usage prevention: idempotency and accounting correctness for retries/timeouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem summary:
Customers and internal billing audits have observed rare but material duplicate usage records leading to double billing. Root causes correlate with at-least-once ingestion paths: client retries after timeouts, network retransmits, and backend consumer reprocessing during transient failures. These duplicates manifest as repeated tokens/embedding units in billing streams and show up as immediate overcharges or (more commonly) as downstream reconciliation adjustments that require manual refunds.

Objective:
Design and implement a robust idempotency and duplicate-detection strategy across the API ingestion edge, rate-limiter layer, and usage ledger that: 1) prevents double counting for common retry patterns; 2) minimizes added latency and storage overhead; 3) preserves compatibility with existing clients while enabling stronger guarantees for new/opt-in clients.

Key constraints and requirements:
- Primary correctness goal: prevent duplicate billed units for the same logical request (same customer intent) in the face of client retries and at-least-once delivery semantics.
- API/SDK changes must be backward compatible; we cannot force all existing clients to upgrade immediately.
- Rate limiting and quota enforcement must remain precise; deduplication checks must not be exploitable to bypass quotas.
- Monitoring and reconciliation must detect residual duplicates and support automated crediting where safe.

High-level approach (phased):
Phase 1 — Detection & instrumentation (hotpath, low risk):
- Add high-fidelity tracing and tagging of ingestion events (request_id, X-Idempotency-Key if present, client-generated request fingerprint, producer host, ingestion-offset).
- Add metrics for duplicate-suspected events per-customer (hash collisions, repeated request_id).
- Run a passive dedup detector in parallel to serving path to measure prevalence and false positive rates.

Phase 2 — Soft dedup at edge (best-effort, no schema changes):
- Implement a short-window dedup cache in front of the usage-enqueue step (Redis/KeyDB with local LRU fallback). Cache key = sha256(customer_id + request_fingerprint) with TTL configurable (default 30s).
- If an event matches recent key: mark as DUPLICATE in metadata and drop from immediate billing ingestion; still send an audit event to the passive detector to validate correctness.
- This phase protects against common quick client retries while keeping latency overhead sub-ms for cache hits.

Phase 3 — Idempotent write path & ledger semantics (stronger guarantee):
- Require/encourage X-Idempotency-Key on billed API endpoints (CreateCompletion, Embeddings). New SDKs will set UUIDs by default; header optional for legacy.
- On write to billing ledger, perform an idempotency check using a durable idempotency store (partitioned by customer_id) with TTL of 7 days for long-running operations. Write path becomes: check-store -> conditional-insert (CAS) -> emit usage event. Ensure the conditional insert is atomic w.r.t. the ledger append (transactional or via monotonic sequence).
- Represent each ledger entry with an idempotency_key + ingestion_id pair; ledger dedup id is enforced in append logic.

Phase 4 — Reconciliation & corrective actions:
- Keep an offline reconciler that groups events by (customer_id, idempotency_key, fingerprint) across the ingestion window and detects duplicates that bypass online layers.
- Automated remediation for low-risk cases: issue offsetting credits in the next billing cycle with clear audit trail. High-risk cases create customer support tickets for manual review.
- Add a customer-facing audit API so customers can query raw usage events and idempotency metadata for disputed charges.

Edge cases and trade-offs:
- TTL selection: longer TTL reduces duplicate risk for retries spread hours apart but increases metadata storage and potential for legitimate repeat requests being blocked. Defaulting to 7 days on durable idempotency store with opt-in per-customer is a compromise.
- Collisions: use 256-bit fingerprints (sha256) + include timestamp bucket for streaming requests to reduce false dedup probability. Monitor collision rate and surface as alert.
- Rate limiter interactions: dedup decisions should not allow bypassing quota checks. We attach quota tokens to logical requests keyed to idempotency_key; repeated attempts within TTL should not consume additional quota.
- Backpressure / latency impact: online durable idempotency checks may add ~1–5ms; benchmarked in Phase 2 to ensure SLA. Provide feature flag to disable strong-idempotency for customers who prefer lower p99 latency.

Implementation details (components):
- API layer: accept X-Idempotency-Key and compute request_fingerprint fallback (customer+model+prompt_hash+params). Inject idempotency metadata into request context.
- Edge Dedup Cache: Redis cluster with partitioning by customer shard; short TTL (30s) for quick retry protection. Local LRU for single-node fallback in case of Redis outage.
- Durable Idempotency Store: append-optimized KV (CockroachDB table or Dynamo-style) storing idempotency_key -> (ingestion_id, created_at, status). Use conditional writes and a background GC to expire keys.
- Billing Ledger: append-only ledger that enforces ledger-level dedup constraint on idempotency_key. If CAS fails (key exists), return existing ingestion_id to client and do not double-count.
- Reconciler: Spark/Flink job that computes duplicate sets and triggers credits/tickets.

Acceptance criteria:
- No duplicates for synthetic retry tests covering common patterns (immediate retry, retry after 200–500ms, retried after backend transient) for 99.999% of requests.
- Duplicate-charge rate in production must drop to < 0.001% of billed events within 2 weeks of soft rollout for enrolled customers.
- Latency impact p50 increase < 2ms and p99 increase < 10ms for idempotent endpoints with strong-idempotency enabled.
- All remedial credit actions must include pre/post usage snapshots and be traceable via a ticket.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for idempotency-store CAS logic and collision handling.
- Integration tests: simulate replayed ingestion, partition failover, consumer reprocessing; assert single ledger entry per idempotency_key.
- Chaos tests: drop idempotency-store writes mid-request, restart consumers, ensure reconciler converges and creates exactly one active billed entry or an automated credit.
- Load tests: measure redis dedup cache hit rate and latency under 10k rps model token generation.
- Backward compatibility tests: legacy clients without X-Idempotency-Key fall back to fingerprint-based dedup; ensure no functional regression.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: deploy passive detector and instrumentation; collect baseline for 2 weeks.
- Week 2: enable soft dedup cache behind feature flag for 10% traffic weighted by customer size (prefer repeat-prone patterns).
- Week 4: enable durable idempotency writes for new SDK clients (opt-in) and run reconciliation in dry-run mode for legacy traffic.
- Week 6–8: expand durable idempotency to all traffic with feature flag off-by-default; enable for customers who opt-in or have higher risk SLA.
- Post-rollout: run retro-credit job for confirmed duplicates during migration window and provide customer-facing incident summaries.

Monitoring and alerts:
- Metric: duplicates_detected_rate (per-customer, per-endpoint). Alert if > 0.01% sustained over 1h for any top-50 customer.
- Metric: idempotency_store_write_errors. Alert on >0.1% error rate.
- Dashboards: top duplicate fingerprints, top customers by duplicate count, reconciler backlog.

Open decisions and follow-ups:
- Final TTL for durable idempotency store (default 7 days vs configurable per-customer).
- Durable store implementation choice: CockroachDB (strong consistency) vs Dynamo-style eventually consistent store with leader election for partition. Engineering to evaluate latency/cost trade-offs (ENG-4822).
- UX for customers to opt into long TTL idempotency and trade latency for stronger protection (PM owns pricing/sla implications).

acceptance_criteria: Synthetic replay tests produce single ledger entry per logical request for 99.999% cases.
Production duplicate-charge rate < 0.001% for enrolled customers within 2 weeks of rollout.
Latency impact within agreed SLOs (p50 +2ms, p99 +10ms).
Automated credits/reconciler run creates audit trail for every corrective action.
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store CAS and lookup behavior.
Integration tests across API edge, Redis cache, durable idempotency store, and ledger append.
Chaos experiments to simulate partial writes and consumer replays.
Load tests to validate cache sizing and latency at expected peak throughput.
